turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: HOY BCS reports that part of the Hotel San Cristóbal in Punta Lobos near Todos Santos was partly demolished on November 10.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Waves had eroded the seawall until the foundations of a two-storey building were exposed. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Punta Lobos fishers had warned since 2015 that the Tres Santos development alters beach dynamics.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They asked for a federal review after Hurricane Polo, but there is still no official technical report.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That long without a report?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The state recorded 187,152 million pesos in constant GDP for 2024, up 3.5 percent from 2023.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That growth figure comes from the economy guide, yet coastal projects keep running into these exact risks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This hits the tourism economy right where projects meet the coast. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It matters for Baja California Sur because any setback there ripples through jobs and investment along the corridor.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wait—how do the fishers' warnings from 2015 connect to the missing technical report today?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: You're listening to Radio BCS2050.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Today's topic is the Economy.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The question we will answer is how the state's overall growth picture looks when these coastal risks are factored in.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: HOY BCS reports that on November 10 part of the Hotel San Cristóbal in Punta Lobos, Todos Santos, was demolished after waves eroded the seawall and exposed the foundations of a two-storey building.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The fishers there had warned since 2015 that the Tres Santos development was changing beach dynamics.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly, and they asked for a federal review after Hurricane Polo, but there is still no official technical report on the causes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That matters for the local economy because the hotel and the beachfront support tourism jobs in an area already feeling the pressure from development.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Now shift to La Paz ranch communities. Palabra BCS covered Governor Víctor Castro’s visit on October 25 to Texcalama, San Andrés, Horconcitos and Saltito de los García.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He promised road repairs, a fixed water tanker in Texcalama by late January, and solar equipment fixes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: He also said he would look at the roughly 50 km road loop called La Herradura de la Sierra that links the ranches.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: For the rural economy these commitments could cut transport costs and keep small producers connected to markets in La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here is the tension: many of these communities have waited years for basic services that directly affect their ability to earn a living.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right. What would you ask the governor about the timeline on that water tanker?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I would ask whether the January deadline includes a maintenance plan so the tankers do not break down again by March.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Good point. Now the safety side. Tribuna de México reported that on October 20 a high-pressure release of cryogenic oxygen at the Infra plant in Pueblo Nuevo forced the evacuation of the David Peralta Osuna secondary school.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The fire chief noted they have been called to the site several times and that urban growth has now surrounded the plant with homes and schools.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Authorities are reviewing relocation of the company, which is an industrial operation that employs people but now sits inside a residential zone.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: For the economy that raises questions about long-term operating costs and insurance if the plant stays or has to move.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Last item. Peninsular Digital says fishers and tourism operators in Los Cabos are preparing an amparo against new port fees set by ASIPONA.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Mar Azul cooperative federation and other marina users say the fees were approved without consultation and raise costs for fishing and nautical tourism.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They want a dialogue table and a review of berthing charges.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That directly hits the daily economics of small boat owners who already face fuel and maintenance costs.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So across these four stories we see tourism infrastructure at risk, rural investment promises, industrial safety questions, and port fee disputes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Each one touches the same underlying question of how Baja California Sur balances growth with the practical needs of the people who keep the economy running.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep thinking about the fishers who warned years ago about Punta Lobos. [pause] Their experience shows how local knowledge often arrives before the technical reports.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: HOY BCS reported on 11 November that crews demolished part of the Hotel San Cristóbal at Punta Lobos in Todos Santos after waves exposed its foundations.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The article says local fishers had warned since 2015 that the Tres Santos development was changing beach dynamics.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: No official technical report exists yet on the exact cause.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That leaves the coastal economy exposed without clear answers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: This matters for the economy because Punta Lobos sits inside La Paz municipality, which lists 2905974532 pesos in its 2026 revenue law.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Los Cabos, by comparison, lists 7421559352 pesos in the same law [chuckle].

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos also holds the largest population at 351111 people and the SJD airport cluster.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its constraints include aquifers 0317 and 0319 already in deficit.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Todos Santos falls under La Paz and carries its own aquifer 0313 in deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mm. So any tourism revenue there hits those water limits first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: On 25 October, Palabra BCS covered Governor Víctor Castro visiting ranch communities in La Paz municipality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: He committed to road repairs, a fixed water tanker in Texcalama by late January, and solar equipment.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: He also promised to assess a 50-kilometre road loop called La Herradura de la Sierra.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That infrastructure could ease daily access for the 292241 people counted in La Paz.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: La Paz has the lowest municipal poverty rate recorded at 20.6 percent in 2020.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Wait—how does that compare once you add the coastal pressure from Todos Santos?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Comondú lists 817244119 pesos in its 2026 revenue law and focuses on the Valle Santo Domingo agro pole.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its population is 73021 people across 589 localities.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Mulegé lists 357354826 pesos from the federal anexo I33 and relies on fisheries and salt.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Loreto lists 263961262 pesos from the same federal transfer and holds the Bahía de Loreto protected area.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: All five municipalities face water or planning limits that cap how far tourism and agro revenue can grow.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The question left open is whether the new infrastructure commitments will reach the coastal and ranch economies before the deficits tighten further.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Exactly. The practical next step is seeing how those January water fixes line up with the existing deficits.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Gringo Gazette reports Los Cabos sent a 2027 revenue law of 6,746 million pesos to the state congress.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is down from the modified 2026 budget.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Own-source revenue from property tax and transfer fees would drop nearly 20 percent to 3,338 million pesos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The city links the shortfall directly to the cooling real estate market.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Meganoticias adds that the state has kept the Camina Cabo walkability plan and the downtown Cabo San Lucas makeover on hold.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Business owners say the projects had Fiturca funds but received no explanation for the pause.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Tribuna de México notes Baja California Sur lost 1.1 percent of formal jobs year on year through October.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The state recorded 1,539 fewer IMSS-registered positions than the prior September.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: NTCD reports the National Employment Service still delivered 48,000 pesos in equipment to eight micro-entrepreneurs in Loreto and Mulegé.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One recipient is in Loreto and seven are in Santa Rosalía, Guerrero Negro, Isla Natividad and San Ignacio.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's earlier Foresight editions already flagged coastal erosion from El Niño between Punta Lobos and San Carlos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They also noted the Sea of Cortez forum's call to double the regional economy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The knowledge graph shows CONAGUA data for aquifer 0313 Todos Santos at a deficit of 2.964513 cubic hectometres per year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Aquifer 0314 El Pescadero shows a small surplus, yet the legal balance does not offset deficits elsewhere.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The state urban programme lists the 2018 La Paz population-centre plan and the 2008 Todos Santos–Pescadero subregional programme as still in force.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those documents set the infrastructure rules that now shape revenue and job numbers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But here is the thread that connects them all.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The stalled downtown projects and the real-estate slowdown sit on top of the same water-balance limits that the aquifer data already record.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The surprise is that the forum's growth target runs into those exact limits without new supply lines or updated urban rules.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the 9 percent revenue drop and the 1.1 percent job loss both trace back to the same documented constraints on water and land use.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The small equipment grants in Loreto and Mulegé show one short-term workaround.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They do not change the underlying balance the state urban programme still carries forward.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: INEGI reports Baja California Sur posted constant-price GDP of 187,152 million pesos in 2024.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That single number already tells us the state economy kept growing.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It rose 3.5 percent from 2023.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Right. Most of that came from the terciarias sector.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Terciarias covers services. Hotels, restaurants, transport and retail.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So every room booked in Cabo San Lucas feeds straight into that total.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal lists labor poverty at 13.2 percent for the fourth quarter of 2024.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The lowest rate among all 32 entities at that moment.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Lower labor poverty usually means more households cover basic needs without falling behind.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: At the same time formal IMSS employment dipped 1.1 percent year-on-year by October.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the overall economy grew while registered jobs edged down slightly.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That tension shows up across the reported figures.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 2024 economic census counted 43,405 establishments.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those are the concrete places where the GDP number actually happens.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same census recorded 300,857 people working in them.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A large base of small and medium businesses.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: In the second quarter of 2026 the economically active population reached its reported level.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Unemployment sat at 2.3 percent.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The headline growth figure sits next to a still-low but slightly softer jobs count.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: IMSS still listed 224,460 formal posts in September.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is the registered workforce the state relies on day to day.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: BCS also attracted 1,353 million dollars in FDI during 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The figure rose to 1,578 million dollars the following year.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: IMCO notes the state climbed from eighth to fifth place in competitiveness rankings between 2021 and 2026.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That ranking tracks how easy it is to do business across the state.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: [chuckle] I keep wondering what that 3.5 percent growth feels like for someone running a small shop in Todos Santos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The numbers are useful, yet they still leave room for questions about daily life.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: CONAGUA published the disponibilidad media anual for BCS aquifers in the DOF 2023 under NOM-011.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That figure is the legal water balance for each aquifer, not a physical measurement.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Aquifer 0313 Todos Santos shows a deficit of 2.964513 hm³ per year, and it covers La Paz municipality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Really? That legal balance then feeds straight into project checks.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Aquifer 0314 El Pescadero shows a small surplus of 0.107682 hm³ per year for La Paz and Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: A surplus cannot move to cover another aquifer though.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The state urban programme from 2024 lists the active plans that must use these DMA numbers when checking project viability.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those plans include the La Paz population-centre urban plan of 2018 and the Todos Santos–Pescadero subregional programme of 2008.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The ontology ties the DMA directly to the viability package for any new hotel, desaladora or industrial park.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The package also checks energy from CFE and PRODESEN plus the POERBCS and PDU instruments. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos General Directorate of Economic Development, led by C. Abril I. Urueta Martínez from 2024 to 2027, works inside that same graph.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The scorecard still marks the East Cape quantitative load as incomplete, even though DMA 0318 and the ANP sit on the graph.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: A surplus in one aquifer cannot offset a deficit in another; each balance stands alone.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That rule shapes where new settlement pressure can actually land without new water sources.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Families are consulted on the coupled factors before any viability sign-off.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The hidden design is simply the requirement that every new economic project must clear the full list of those documented balances first.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would change if the East Cape load numbers were finally added to the graph? [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Directorate would have one more concrete check before approving the next hotel or road link.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And the state programme already lists the exact instruments that would apply that check.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the everyday permit for a new building starts with those aquifer lines in the DOF.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s Vision for the economy opens with what INEGI already measured.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Constant-price GDP reached 187,152 million pesos in 2024.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And it rose 3.5 percent from the year before.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Really? That growth sits right next to the CNIE numbers on foreign direct investment.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: 1,353 million dollars came in during 2024.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Then it moved to 1,578 million the next year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: At the same time IMSS data show formal employment fell 1.1 percent year-on-year by October.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: With 224,460 posts recorded in September.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal treats any 3.5 percent annual goal and talk of tripling regional FDI as outside proposals from forums.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Not as its own projections. So the risk it flags is that growth continues yet stays uneven.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And part of the investment story remains a proposal rather than a measured path.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The aspiration the portal sets out is a polycentric, regenerative economy.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Where investment does not simply clone the Cabos model everywhere.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Formal employment would not depend on one coastal vocation alone. [chuckle]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Tendencia 2050 reading that still holds describes distinct roles instead of one repeated formula.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos stays the tourism engine but under water and power stress.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: East Cape sits in tension with protected areas. Todos Santos and El Pescadero form the Pacific amenity spine.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: La Paz would act as the services capital and water-energy node.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Loreto functions as a tourism-conservation anchor. Comondú keeps its role as an agricultural hub with relatively more room.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Northern Mulegé appears as a thinly documented corridor now carrying a remote generation tender.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal’s levers are to give weight to La Paz, Comondú and the north without pretending every place can copy the same engine.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Read formal employment and inflation together with the actual water and grid ceilings.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Do not treat any forum goal such as tripling FDI as an already accepted projection.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The conditions listed are straightforward. Each vocation keeps its distinct role.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: New tourism or residential growth appears only where water and energy show evidenced margin or a non-DMA source such as desal.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: East Cape and Loreto must respect ANP and POEL ceilings before scaling hospitality.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Comondú and the north add production or energy without emptying services or protected areas.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: On the watchlist sits the 2027 budget package of 28.3 billion pesos.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Approval expected in December. The fifth report was delivered to Congress on 12 November.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The public event is set for 27 November at Plaza de la Reforma in La Paz.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would it take for the state to move from the present mixed signals toward that polycentric pattern?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal leaves that open, but the demand-supply board already shows the state-scale constraints that any path must respect. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That contrast stands out right away.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos projects a revenue drop next year as the real estate market cools, and fishers there are preparing a legal challenge over the new port fees.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Meanwhile the governor visited ranch communities near La Paz and committed to roads, water, temporary jobs and solar power.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Business owners in Los Cabos say the state has paused the Camina Cabo walkability plan and the downtown makeover.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those commitments and the job numbers together suggest responsibility rests with state leadership to broaden opportunities beyond one sector.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What remains unknown is whether the legal challenge will succeed or how the proposed relocation of the Infra plant will affect local schools.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The takeaway is that formal employment in BCS remains tied to a narrow set of activities, and the documented findings leave open how quickly that pattern can shift.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: I keep wondering what the ranch communities will see first from those commitments. [pause]
